qualified_cases.owner_probe: Bytes::from_owner over a dedicated Vec with Drop counter and Notify. The raw HTTP/2 peer drains all DATA into its own receive-copy storage, then withholds the first response. Over-budget client shared owner must drop while the call remains pending; bounded identity requests keep it until terminal outcome.

matrix.scenario: Default unlimited encoding, 4 MiB + 1 identity bytes, retryable trailers-only UNAVAILABLE, logging disabled/enabled: one first send, owner released before response, zero retries.
Exactly 4 MiB identity payload: three identical wire frames, one encoding, retained owner until terminal success.
Explicit outbound cap 4 MiB + 1 permits retention and three attempts for that payload.
Compressible 4 MiB + 1 original payload, unlimited outbound: gzip frame fits the actual replay budget and retries three times without re-encoding.
Deterministic incompressible 4 MiB original payload, explicit 4 MiB outbound cap: gzip wire payload exceeds the cap, first send accepted and committed against replay.
Over-budget configured identity frame followed by REFUSED_STREAM: one attempt, no transparent replacement, shared owner released before reset.
Unconfigured 4 MiB + 1 identity payload followed by REFUSED_STREAM: existing transparent replacement remains, two identical frames and one encoding.
Over-budget configured identity first send succeeds normally and releases shared owner before the response.

common_assertions: Actual encoded payload versus frozen budget checked at the held-response boundary.
Compression flag/header and complete wire bytes agree across attempts.
No re-encoding, no phantom/exhausted retry counters; transport byte permits return to zero.
A follow-up call succeeds with max_concurrent_rpcs=1 after every case.

parent_acceptance_review.FL-08: QG-11 through QG-17 jointly cover response commitment during completed/stalled uploads, encode-once frames, explicit policy/unknown side-effect histories, terminal admission reclamation, released routing load during backoff, dispatch-based retry counting and finite policy replay payload retention.
parent_acceptance_review.seeded_scope: QG-14 retains 32 seeded histories (16 seeds with/without policy), rerun by both default/all-feature retry_safety here. This does not qualify a fleet retry storm, the full upstream profile, or exactly-once execution.
parent_acceptance_review.remaining_owner: FL-09 remains pending for outage amplification/recovery-load and jitter/throttling qualification; this card does not satisfy its rpc-bench check.

limits: No new public API, dependencies, unsafe code, numeric limit values or global outbound defaults.

The owner probe qualifies the dedicated shared payload allocation in identity requests. Compressed requests release the original source before upload; their encoded budget and forbidden/eligible replay are checked by observed wire length and actual attempt counts, not a global allocator probe.
The focused five-test run precedes the final compression-header and observed-budget assertion tightening; both complete default/all-feature retry suites qualify those final assertions.
Interop covers the pinned registry plaintext cases. Eight Go compression rows are explicitly unsupported; no full release, cloud, performance or production qualification is claimed.
Unconfigured transparent retry and hedging still have no finite default replay retention cap. Shared backing allocations/segment metadata are outside the logical payload bound.
